correctness.rationale: All extensions are y_j+z_j with z_j in Y-perp. Their dual norm to the q power is sum_j w_j (||y_j||^2+||z_j||^2)^(q/2) and excess norm B^q=sum w_j||z_j||^q. For 1<q<2, the weighted Lq<=L2 inequality applied to normalized coordinates yields 1+B^2<=R^2; equality proportional b_j=sqrt(R^2-1)a_j. At q=2 exact Pythagoras holds. For q>2, allocate excess costs d_j and u_j=w_j||y_j||^q: w_j||z_j||^q=[(u_j+d_j)^(2/q)-u_j^(2/q)]^(q/2). This is decreasing in u_j and has nondecreasing F_u(d)/d, giving maximum at u*=min_j u_j and a concentrated cost if u*>0, otherwise on zero-weight-of-phi atoms. Symmetry Phi0 +/- Z proves diameter twice maximum radius. Checked actual deterministic checker source; independent q=4 two-atom optimization matched the algebraic formula, while finite sampling is not proof.
